short_description: Construction runtime recovery, late-interest synchronization and replication-scale policy over accepted T1A.6 runtime networking.
purpose: Make canonical Construction runtime survive recovery/reconnect and replicate only relevant runtime state at scale while reusing existing persistence, authority and interest foundations instead of creating domain-private global infrastructure.
expected_outcome: Recovered runtime state preserves canonical revisions and effects, reconnect/late-interest clients converge from authoritative baselines, irrelevant constructs are not replicated, and scale behavior is bounded without changing permanent identity or authority ownership.
progress_note: T1A.7.3 focused Windows validation PASSED on local checkout c6544100564d2fa55d96b607ccd9ea61c01387b1 with runtime/test boundary cab2e1cdcafd831ab9c0cb09123383bf96f5dfe0. Inherited gates remained green: T1A.4 153, C5B 32, T1A.5 67, transactional 36, T1A.7.1 recovery 60, NX0 150, M3 77, C5C 29, T1A.6 multiplayer 25/0, T1A.7.2 interest binding 34 and late-interest/reconnect 35. New T1A.7.3 selective planner passed 44 assertions and real selective M3 process acceptance passed 35 assertions. Two transient Parse JSON failed messages came from polling result files during concurrent rewrite; subsequent polls succeeded and both affected suites completed PASS, so this is non-blocking harness read-race noise rather than runtime/network failure. Full world/core regression remains required on the same local checkout without fetch/reset.
